prior_own_findings_disposition.status: closed in selected source by static producer-to-consumer verification
prior_own_findings_disposition.evidence: serve constructs the nonsecret reserved resource overlay from the validated owner's ResourceProfile, composes the ToolPlan environment and live Git token, and sends the exact owner tool-bin path. execute reconstructs the shim PATH from that owner path plus inherited native PATH, removes foreign Git routing variables, then applies the granted environment before OwnedProcess::spawn. TMPDIR, output, cache, port and compose/cookie namespace values therefore no longer come solely from a mutable caller environment. Authentication/native settings are not copied into the IPC DTO.
prior_own_findings_disposition.controls_read_not_run: The new actual built-rrx shim subprocess fixture deliberately overrides TMPDIR and CARGO_TARGET_DIR with sibling paths, observes a pre-commit helper's final temp/cache environment, uses real nested shim Git reentry, and verifies sibling namespaces/HEAD remain unchanged. This source inspection is not independent execution or mutation credit.

checked_source_facts.evidence: The server admits a candidate index only for Git with a live parent lease, resolves the canonical exact own Git admin parent and finite index/index.lock/next-index-N forms, then restores that validated GIT_INDEX_FILE after shim routing removal. Candidate-index hook reentry uses the same live owned lease. Detached checkout is now rejected in the finite managed form parser. This is a cooperative shim policy, not enforcement against raw absolute commands or hostile same-user actions.

Core::run retains only finite nonsecret NativeFailure categories; bootstrap auth/capability/metadata/protocol/transport conditions carry explicit categories, errors produce Unknown work rather than native success, and current terminal publication records the category. Cancellation wins without a late known outcome reopening its generation. Newly read fixtures cover seven Codex bootstrap categories and verify no native_input intent/raw fixture error retention. They were not executed.

Work is persisted before stop_and_reap hygiene. Group signaling errors are separate cleanup diagnostics; cleanup is still Unknown with explicit escaped-process and Docker reconciliation gaps. Session terminal labels and owned-process receipts are not a whole-workload death or resource-release certificate. No descendant-death or universal same-user isolation guarantee is inferred.

begin_execution_epoch loads open units through strict indexed/body unit_tx validation, fences both native-effects and result-finalization permissions, preserves already known Success/Failure, converts genuinely unobserved work to Unknown, schedules cleanup and invalidates active executor generation projection atomically.

fence_epoch_sessions checks managed mapping, exact Record/body scope/id/provider/worktree agreement, leaves existing terminal observations unchanged, and converts other managed Sessions to Lost with unknown dispatch state. It does not adopt stored PID signaling authority or invent a native completion.

fence_epoch_effects validates pending effect identity/scope and CASes Pending to Unknown with a finite runtime_epoch_lost receipt. It preserves previously settled states. The epoch transaction clears old quota active/probe/waiter scheduling projections. No pending effect is replayed or marked confirmed merely by restart.

Committed tests exercise known-success preservation, live and previously logically retired Session/effect fencing, old-authority rejection, fresh generation/path admission, quota waiter/lease reset, and body/index corruption causing epoch transaction rollback. They were read, not executed.

Codex usedPercent remains conservatively decoded: negative/unavailable estimates are Unknown, values at/above 100 indicate exhaustion without fabricated remaining capacity, and out-of-normal percentages do not become valid estimates. This source behavior is not actual provider conformance.

The writer-function registration was extracted without adding a production public bypass; current-writer corruption helpers are cfg(test)/test support. Historical-schema controls reconstruct old schemas rather than falsely relabel a schema4 database as schema3. The current source guards remain connection-local writer-contract fences.

reports.review_kind: STRICT preliminary Phase2 component source review, round 5

findings.title: Claude's recognized authentication failure is converted into completed work failure
findings.evidence: RunState::observe explicitly returns AdapterError(AuthenticationUnavailable) for an owned unsuccessful result containing 'not logged in', 'authentication failed', or 'invalid api key'. Core::claude then checks only seen.is_err(), owned result identity, is_error and a recognized terminal subtype. For an initialized error_during_execution result it returns Ok(Failure, Completed, frame) unless a recognized exhausted bucket exists, swallowing that typed authentication error. Core::run treats every Ok tuple as failure=None, and finish_execution_with_failure persists work=failure, disposition=completed, native_failure=null. Even outside this catch-all terminal path, AdapterError kinds are not mapped by Core::run's NativeFailure-only downcast, so Claude UnsupportedCapability becomes ProtocolFailure.
findings.impact: The new named failure API is accurate for the Codex bootstrap fixtures but not for the Claude producer. Consumers cannot distinguish a login/capability prerequisite failure from unsuccessful Task work, or supply the named reason promised by the design; the failed-work finalization permission is also left open.

contract_evidence.requirement: Authentication errors and unsupported metadata remain named; definitive unrelated native work failures remain failures.

findings.proposed_control: Inspect the Claude AdapterError kind before the generic unsuccessful-work fallback, translate finite AuthenticationUnavailable/UnsupportedCapability/ownership-or-protocol categories into the bounded NativeFailure taxonomy, and retain only the finite category in status/audit. Preserve genuine ProcessFailure work terminals separately. Do not retain raw authentication text.
causal_controls_to_add: Account-free owned Claude fixture: successful initialization, own system/init, then error_during_execution + is_error=true + result='Not logged in'. Assert named AuthenticationUnavailable, a non-completed disposition, native_failure audit category and no retained raw text.
Account-free unsupported Claude control request fixture: assert UnsupportedCapability rather than ProtocolFailure.
Negative control: ordinary initialized non-auth work error remains known Failure, Completed.
findings.verification: Verified by immutable-source control flow only; no tests or native account runs performed.
findings.prior_finding_relation: Round4 M2 is partially fixed: named Codex bootstrap failures and persisted finite categories are added, but the Claude path remains incomplete.

findings.title: Unclassified terminal limit errors are irreversibly recorded as normal work failure
findings.evidence: Claude's error_during_execution terminal is QuotaInterrupted only when an accepted Exhausted bucket has also been observed during this run; otherwise the catch-all returns Failure/Completed. Unknown or omitted Claude rate-limit type/status returns no observation, and no separate terminal limit-like classification exists. Codex similarly records every failed terminal other than the exact usageLimitExceeded discriminator as Failure/Completed. Therefore an owned terminal indicating a transient/unknown limit, without confirmed subscription metadata, is not represented as Unknown with bounded capacity recheck. finish_execution_with_failure commits known work failure and wait_reason=None, so a future scheduler cannot simply resume a waiting unit from that producer result.
findings.impact: A missing/new quota shape or non-subscription transient terminal limit can fail Task work instead of waiting for bounded capacity recheck. This is a defect in the existing terminal producer, independent of the still-unconnected Workflow/CLI scheduling integration. Text or HTTP 429 still must not be asserted as confirmed subscription exhaustion.

contract_evidence.requirement: Unclassified terminal limit-like errors record work unknown and WaitingCapacity with bounded diagnostic/recheck; they are not labelled confirmed subscription exhaustion or successful work.

findings.proposed_control: Add a finite unclassified-capacity terminal outcome, separate from confirmed subscription exhaustion and definitive work errors. Persist Unknown plus the explicit capacity wait/recheck reason before native retirement; keep confirmed_subscription false and ensure fresh-attempt recovery cannot blindly replay old native input. Do not make every failed terminal or arbitrary 429 a confirmed quota event.
causal_controls_to_add: Account-free Claude fixture: initialized owned error_during_execution with a terminal limit indication and no recognized rate_limit_event; assert Unknown + unclassified capacity wait, not known Failure and not confirmed subscription exhaustion.
Repeat with an unknown rateLimitType and with an unknown structured Codex terminal limit discriminator; assert bounded wait/recheck and no fabricated quota balance.
Negative controls: known max-turn/budget caps and definitive ordinary work errors remain failures; auth failures keep their named prerequisite category; confirmed quota errors still use WaitingQuota.
findings.verification: Verified by immutable-source exhaustiveness of terminal branches. No claim that any particular real CLI version emits the suggested synthetic fixture; native observation/qualification remains unverified.
findings.prior_finding_relation: New finding on an existing terminal producer; not absence of future Workflow integration.

prior_own_round4_dispositions.subject: Bootstrap diagnostics were erased as Unknown/Lost
prior_own_round4_dispositions.evidence: native.rs:786-804 classifies bounded NativeFailure categories, 816-820 persists the category and state/execution.rs:645-646 audits it. Codex bootstrap explicitly labels auth/capability/metadata failures. New Claude bootstrap loop observes cancellation/authority before input dispatch. Residual typed Claude error conversion and terminal authentication fallback are recorded as current M1.
prior_own_round4_dispositions.verification: Source and committed fixture assertions inspected only; tests not executed.

positive_source_observations: begin_execution_epoch uses one Immediate transaction; open native/finalization authorities are closed, known work/disposition are retained, unknown work is marked lost, matching active executor projections are generation-fenced, and cleanup jobs are queued (state/execution.rs:362-422).
Epoch recovery reconciles managed Session bindings even for already-retired units, preserving historical PID as diagnostic rather than signal authority (state/execution/sessions.rs:190-229).
Pending effects become Unknown with a bounded runtime_epoch_lost receipt and version change; confirmed history is not blindly replayed (state/execution/effects.rs:1-28).
Quota leases/probe pointers/waiters are cleared at the epoch boundary; existing resource namespaces stay retained rather than being recycled.

The added epoch tests assert known-result preservation, cancellation disposition preservation, stale authority rejection, fresh namespace/generation and transaction rollback on indexed/body mismatch. These assertions were read, not run.
Grant namespace_environment is enforced by the actual child grant; Task tool_bin is prepended without transporting native stdio/authentication through Runtime.
